title: Vitello Tonnato
subtitle: Cold sliced veal or beef with tuna and caper sauce
excerpt: An Italian summer classic that sounds improbable -- cold sliced meat under a creamy tuna and anchovy sauce. It is served at room temperature and gets better the longer it sits. A northern Italian summer staple for dinner parties and buffets alike.
sourceNotes: Vitello tonnato is the great Piedmontese summer antipasto. Cold sliced veal dressed with a tuna mayonnaise is a combination dating back to 19th century cookbooks. The dish is served at room temperature, never warm.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. The flavour improves after a day in the fridge. Add extra capers before serving.

content.text: Poach the meat gently -- boiling makes it tough and dry. The water should barely tremble. Cool the meat completely in the poaching liquid before slicing. This keeps it moist.

items.prepNote: use 600g veal topside if available -- otherwise use beef silverside or topside
rinsed -- half for the sauce, half to garnish

content.text: Put the meat in a snug saucepan with the carrot, celery, onion, bay leaves and peppercorns. Cover with cold water. Bring very slowly to a bare simmer. Cook gently for 50 to 60 minutes. The meat should be just cooked through but still slightly pink. Let it cool completely in the liquid.
While the meat cools, make the sauce. Put the tuna, anchovies, half the capers, lemon juice, mustard and egg yolks in a blender. Blend until smooth.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the olive oil in a thin stream. The sauce will emulsify and thicken to a pourable cream. If too thick, add a tablespoon of cold water. Taste and season.
Slice the cooled meat very thin -- about 3mm. Arrange on a wide serving platter in overlapping layers.
Spoon the tuna sauce over the meat, covering it completely. Scatter the remaining capers over the top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving.
Serve at room temperature, not cold from the fridge. Add a final drizzle of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon.

items.cause: Boiled too hard or cooled out of the liquid
items.fix: The water must barely simmer. Cool the meat in the poaching liquid -- this keeps it moist. Thin slicing also helps.

items.cause: Oil added too fast during blending
items.fix: Add the oil in a very thin, slow stream with the blender running. If it splits, start fresh yolks in a clean bowl and slowly drizzle in the split sauce while whisking.

content.text: Vitello tonnato is from Piedmont in northern Italy. It is served cold at summer antipasto spreads. The tuna-meat combination is very old. It is better made 24 hours ahead.
